comments.content:
Could I potentially be of help with this?
I only ask because I worked on https://github.com/ubiquity/.github/pull/112 which was the most thorough attempt at accounting since the inception of the startup, which included hundreds and hundreds of permits that were not included in the DB as far back as 01/01/2024. (`// ~3yrs ago 29/05/2024` is a comment in my code, so I had validated on-chain as far back as then being `2021`)
I spent hours manually checking amounts and verifying nulled permits as well as programmatically verifying them on-chain as well. 
---
If it helps you @v4d33m I can run the script from https://github.com/ubiquity/.github/pull/112 and send you over the data
lmk I'm happy to assist.
I'm out at the moment but I should be free later tonight to sort it out no worries

1. I updated the script a little to include the most recent funding wallet but I'm sure there was one or two between that and the ones used at the time when I wrote that code, so I expect a few to be missing.
2. The DB/CSV has 795 permits. My DB was seeded from a backup last year so I'm unsure how many are in now as I no longer have access to the backups to assess.
3. The script pulls more permits from issues than it does from on-chain about ~60 of difference.
4. It does not account for the issue that came to light regarding foo's permits being generated for an incorrect wallet for however long that was going on for.
5. I have pushed all of the data that the script gathers into the repo in case any of that might help you.
6. My script verifies both `claimed` and `unclaimed` or does it's best to. Below is a screenshot of the two leaderboards side by side (they can be found in the repo alongside the other data) to show the drastic difference without validating on-chain. I'm not sure if the prod DB now handles all of these edge cases and scenarios but I hope this helps.
7. [`unspent-permits.json`](https://github.com/Keyrxng/ubq-.github/blob/refactor/v2/airdrop-cli/src/scripts/data/dc-unspent-permits.json) is a JSON of permits which have been generated but unclaimed according to the script.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73ace22d-8027-4264-956c-504299743473)
[permits_rows .csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19041953/permits_rows.csv)
https://github.com/Keyrxng/ubq-.github/tree/refactor/v2/airdrop-cli/src/scripts/data
##### Cool to see I'm now in 2nd place for claimed, 3rd for unclaimed. I was stuck at 4th the last time I ran this

I'm not sure if the DB schema has changed, it sounds like it has although you could match using the `beneficiary_id` with the `wallet` & `users` tables possibly but I can tweak it no problem.
- Add two new columns, collect `tx.from` and `tx.to`
- Does the `created` timestamp matter for you? I could likely use the timestamp of the on-chain transaction or when the permit was generated on the issue. Both have their pros and cons I guess.

Following on from TG:
So long as the `transaction` hashes were of use to you, which was the most grueling and time consuming aspect of gathering all the data I did at the time. They were also the main requirement over `created` timestamps due to being a prerequisite of other tasks, the focus was on collecting and validating those.
I was free until 3pm yesterday unfortunately you stopped replying at 1pm without giving me clear enough directions, which I tried to clarify just before 1pm. Which is a shame as it would have taken me no less than 10 minutes to add two new props and re-run the script.
I hope that accommodations can be made if the transaction hashes where of value to your as that was the value my script produced over anything else.
Many thanks.
